cards.anchor: Hypothesis for the eight invented records: exactly K2, K5 and K7 checked, the other five unchecked, zero incorrect-key writes, unchanged source scores and latest S2 loaded within ten simulated minutes.
cards.burden: Nine sequential one-minute actions use available immutable-key replay controls and notebook logging. Capture and resolution are the stipulated inspect/select and key-bound commit operations; no extra verification action is assumed. Production implementation and human benefit remain untested.
cards.construction: Capture each intended checklist key during inspection and retain that immutable token across refresh; commit resolves the token to its key. Replay K2 inspect 0-1, refresh 1-2, commit 2-3; K5 inspect 3-4, refresh 4-5, commit 5-6; K7 inspect 6-7, refresh 7-8, commit 8-9. Refreshes load S1, S2 and S2 respectively. Log every intended key, token and actual write.
cards.defeat: An intact-token replay writing any unintended key, changing source scores, missing the exact final map or S2, or exceeding ten minutes defeats the completion claim. A deliberately corrupted token causing a wrong write defeats any stronger claim that immutable addressing alone preserves intention.
cards.mutation: Replace the row-number selection carrier with an immutable-key carrier; retain the preferred refresh cadence. Treat correct token content as a separate prerequisite from carrier stability.
cards.prediction_candidate: Prospectively, intact tokens write K2, K5 and K7 and satisfy the outcome in nine minutes. Substituting K5 for the intended K7 token after inspection at 6-7 instead predicts writes K2, K5, K5 and K7 remaining unchecked. Equal score 75 cannot detect or repair this intention substitution.
cards.prediction_rival: The rival that per-commit freshness alone ensures correction predicts the row-bound arm also completes correctly. Under the stipulated ordering, the proposed row-bound replay instead predicts writes K5, K7, K7, leaving K2 unchecked; this arm is diagnostic and fails the outcome.
cards.probe: Replay identical snapshots, action times and intended checklist keys in three arms: row binding; intact immutable tokens; immutable tokens with only the final K7 token replaced by K5. Compare tokens, retained rows, intended/actual writes and final maps. The first comparison isolates addressing; the second tests intention integrity. These arms are proposed, not executed.
cards.rival: Refresh freshness is sufficient for target correctness irrespective of selection carrier; a further rival equates stable carrier identity with correct intended identity.
unknowns: No completed key-token replay is supplied.
Real token capture, binding and validation behavior are unknown.
Additional real verification costs could exceed the modeled budget.
Concurrency, deleted keys and load failures are outside the exercise.
The stipulated single miswrite does not establish repeated mismatch-refresh feedback.

cards.anchor: Preserve exact target statuses, zero wrong-key writes, read-only scores, final S2 and the ten-minute ceiling while testing whether intermediate refresh is necessary.
cards.burden: The candidate costs seven simulated minutes using the original row-bound editor. A matched diagnostic pair costs eight minutes per replay. A manual selection-boundary rule and actual-write log suffice within the available synthetic resources; no macro or connector is required.
cards.construction: Retain loaded S0 through three complete inspect/commit pairs: K2 at 0-2, K5 at 2-4 and K7 at 4-6. Refresh only during 6-7, loading S2 and preserving local statuses by key. Permit refresh only after a pending selection has been committed; final freshness is still required.
cards.defeat: Any incorrect-key write, wrong final status, score modification, failure to load S2 or elapsed time above ten defeats the completion hypothesis. If moving refresh across the selection/commit boundary produces equivalent write errors in the matched controls, the proposed boundary mechanism is weakened.
cards.mutation: Move freshness to completed-edit boundaries instead of installing it between selection and commit. Fixed checklist targets permit the original carrier to remain valid until the last write.
cards.prediction_candidate: The seven-minute replay prospectively writes K2, K5, K7 only and completes with S2. In an eight-minute matched pair, the safe ordering predicts the exact target map; refreshing between the first selection and commit predicts a wrong K5 write for intended K2 and K2 remaining unchecked.
cards.prediction_rival: The necessity rival predicts the seven-minute schedule cannot achieve reliable correction without pre-commit refresh. The refresh-count-only rival predicts equivalent correctness for matched controls with two refreshes each, independent of their position relative to selection and commit.
cards.probe: First replay the seven-minute candidate and check every write plus final freshness. Then compare two eight-action schedules: safe inspect K2, commit, refresh, inspect K5, commit, inspect K7, commit, final refresh; risky inspect K2, refresh, commit, inspect K5, commit, inspect K7, commit, final refresh. Each action costs one minute. Both have S1 loaded by minute 3, unchanged subsequent action times and S2 loaded at minute 8. Record the first write separately from later statuses; repaired errors still fail.
cards.rival: Reliable correction necessarily requires a refresh immediately before each commit; alternatively, refresh count explains errors without regard to the retained selection boundary.
unknowns: Candidate completion and the matched comparison remain unexecuted.
The matched pair changes first-commit time as well as refresh placement; identification is bounded by the deterministic stipulated model.
Real editor binding, detection costs and interruption effects are unknown.
No claim covers concurrency, deleted keys, snapshot failures or operational reliability.
